note: Archetype rates, not vendor-specific quotes. Entries cite a tier of model ('mid-tier frontier text model') rather than a named product, because naming one vendor's model would make every estimate on the site wrong the day that vendor repriced. Each archetype is set at a representative published rate for its tier and links to a real rate card so the number can be audited. Costs are computed from this file at build time; no entry stores a cost figure of its own. When a rate here changes, every affected estimate on the site changes with it in one commit.

frontier-large.label: Large frontier text model
frontier-large.note: Top-tier reasoning model. Representative of the most expensive publicly listed general-purpose text APIs.

frontier-mid.label: Mid-tier frontier text model
frontier-mid.note: The default workhorse tier. Most products in this directory are estimated against this unless their task obviously needs more or less.

frontier-small.label: Small fast text model
frontier-small.note: Cheap, low-latency tier used for autocomplete, classification and short-form generation.

frontier-nano.label: Nano text model
frontier-nano.note: The cheapest hosted tier, appropriate for inline completion where latency matters more than depth.

asr-standard.label: Speech-to-text transcription
asr-standard.note: Hosted transcription billed per minute of audio. Self-hosting an open ASR model is cheaper again; see each entry's DIY path.

gpu-hour-highend.label: Rented high-end GPU
gpu-hour-highend.note: A100/H100-class rental, for video and music generation where a mid-range card is not a credible substitute. Used where a product trains its own generative media models and publishes no comparable API.

gpu-hour-commodity.label: Rented commodity GPU
gpu-hour-commodity.note: Mid-range rental GPU (L4/A10 class) for running open weights yourself. Used where a product has no comparable public API and the honest alternative is self-hosting.
